title: The court divides along the sultan's two marriages. Duʿā's family, the Marīnids of Fās, twice made war on the Emirate; Aiman's, the Baḥrī Mamlūks, fight beside it in Sicily, Malta and Catalonia. The Mamlūk commitment is a boon for the Aiman faction

data.aimanFaction: the Mamlūk alliance, Aiman and her son Yūsuf
data.duaFaction: Duʿā, the heir Ismāʿīl, the regency at Gharnāṭa

title: Peace with Aragon and Sicily. Barcelona has been under siege for 282 days and is about to fall; King Joan might still fight on from his Sicilian crown, until the shaykh of Barqa lands 3,000 men on the island and storms Siracusa. Offered peace or a war on Sicily itself, he accepts. Aragon gives up every town it has left, 34 of them from the Pyrenees to the Ebro, and the Kingdom of Aragon ceases to hold land. Malta passes to the Mamlūks, and Sicily pays reparations. The war score stands at +61%

data.reparations: Sicily pays war reparations to Granada
data.passageToPalermo: the envoys' promise that King Joan would be let go unharmed to Palermo: he leaves Aragon alive and free, still king of Sicily, less Malta (Trent's account)
data.siracusa: stormed by Barqa's 3,000 shortly before the peace; returned to Sicily by it (Trent's account; Sicily owns Syracuse after the peace)

warDead.note: battle losses only, from the war's five battles; attrition and the siege of Barcelona are not counted. Barqa also lost 8 ships off Malta

source: saves of 15 March 1375 before and after the peace; Trent's account

title: As the Kingdom of Aragon collapses, so do its outlying lands. Montpellier, beyond the Pyrenees, swears itself to the English rather than the French, and Sassari in Sardinia is taken back by Arborea, the Genoese vassal. The Kingdom of Aragon is no more, at first

data.when: between 1 November 1374 and the peace: both had already changed hands in the save taken just before it
data.note: Aragon held 34 towns on the morning of the peace and none after it; its truce with Granada still runs to 15 March 1388

source: autosave of 1 November 1374; saves of 15 March 1375; Trent's account

title: With Catalonia the realm grows from 60 towns to 94 and from 765,000 souls to 1,275,000. For the first time the Catalans are its largest people, 455,000 against 452,000 Andalusīs, and Christians outnumber the faithful two to one: 815,000 Catholics against 397,000 Muslims and 63,000 Jews. Barcelona, at 46,000, is the realm's third city
source: save of 15 March 1375 after the peace

title: The sultan resolves not to keep Catalonia and Aragon for the crown. They will be made two new ṭāʾifas: Catalonia, and a resurrected Aragon in the interior. Returning Aragonese land to a successor kingdom looks far less aggressive than seizing it outright. In the same reordering, Mursiyya is to be absorbed directly into the crown

data.why: to be seen returning rightful Aragonese land to a successor kingdom rather than seizing it
data.status: carried out the next day, 16 March 1375

source: Trent's account, after the peace of 15 March 1375

title: Mursiyya, one of the first ṭāʾifas, is taken into the crown: its twelve towns, from Murcia and Cartagena to Albacete and Lorca, pass directly to the sultan. Its ḥājiba Dolça is granted lands and titles and confirmed as a governor. The crown's reach there will be limited at first, and the autonomy and friendship of its Catalan court and traders are carefully kept, their institutions accepted within the state rather than ignored

The heir Ismāʿīl, nine, is betrothed to Bernarda of Murcia, eight, the gifted daughter of Dolça and heir of the old ṭāʾifa: Murcia's house is bound to the throne as its land is bound to the crown. One thing to watch: the girl is being raised at the Castilian court for now, though the betrothal holds

data.raisedAt: the Castilian court (she sits in Castile in the save)
data.culture: Castilian, like her father; Murcia's court is tied to the Catalans through its traders (Trent)

title: Two ṭāʾifas are carved from the conquered lands of Aragon. In the east, the Catalans are freed from the Aragonese as a strong Ṭāʾifa of Catalonia: 28 towns and 453,000 people around Barcelona, under Francesc de Montsoriu. In the west, at the edges, a renewed Aragon is proclaimed: six towns and 52,000 people around Benabarre and Monzón, an Islamic state dressed as the old crown's successor, under King Alfons de Borja, whom the game counts the fifth of his name

data.note: ARA is the old Kingdom of Aragon's own tag, landless since the peace of 15 March, now a ṭāʾifa of the sultan

title: The Restoration of al-Andalus. The sultan no longer calls himself a successor: the Emirate of Granada becomes al-Andalus, an empire, one continuation reaching back hundreds of years. Offered the convivencia of the Umayyads or the sword of the Almohads, he chooses the first: let Qurṭuba shine again as the ornament of the world. Tolerance, wealth and learning are to stand level with the Word

data.choice: Let Cordoba shine again as the ornament of the world (against: The sword of the Maghreb shall unite the faithful)
data.unlocks: the convivencia destiny path in the Traditions tab

source: Trent's account and screenshot of the event, 16 March 1375; save of 16 March 1375

title: In the reorganisation of the realm the Emperor's younger sister Maryam, eighteen and the ablest mind at court, is appointed to the dīwān. Aiman, his principal wife, holds no formal seat, since the game bars the consort from the council, but sits there all the same by the strength of the harem

data.consort: Aiman: no formal office (the game bars the consort from the council); a member in the chronicle by the harem's strength (Trent's ruling)
data.action: changing the realm's societal values (from 17 March 1375)

title: A royal marriage binds the house of Naṣr to the new Ṭāʾifa of Catalonia

The truce with Qashtāla runs out, and the Emperor does not wait. The French are pushing the English into the sea; wait, and Rome will rally France to blunt the advance. War is declared on Castile under the Reconquest of Iberia, framed as the restoration of Aragon, and a levy of gold and men is laid on the nobles and the ṭāʾifas

data.framing: the Aragonese restoration: Zaragoza, Huesca, Teruel and the Aragonese heartland, held by Castile
data.levy: on the nobles and the ṭāʾifas, in gold and men (Trent)

title: Rome and Lisbon answer the Castilian call: Portugal, Castile's partner in the union, and the Papal States with their vassals Faenza, Siena and a third. Egypt answers ours, with its vassals
